declarations.RDF11.Dataset.quads: Project the named graphs to name/triple membership. This deliberately records no membership for an empty named graph and omits the separately represented default graph.
declarations.RDF11.Dataset.empty: The dataset with an empty default graph and no named graphs.
declarations.RDF11.Dataset.emptyNamed: The dataset with an empty default graph and exactly one present named graph, whose contents are empty. Classical name equality is used; this is a mathematical definition, not a compiled storage procedure.
declarations.RDF11.Dataset.emptyNamed_present: The chosen name really is present with the empty graph in the one-empty-named-graph dataset.
declarations.RDF11.Dataset.emptyNamed_ne_empty: A dataset with one present empty named graph differs from the dataset with no named graphs.
declarations.RDF11.Dataset.emptyNamed_same_quads: The one-empty-named-graph dataset and the dataset with no named graphs have identical named-quad membership. Quad membership alone loses the presence distinction.
declarations.RDF11.Dataset.eq_of_default_names_quads: Exact default-graph equality, identical sets of present graph names, and identical named-quad membership together imply exact dataset equality. This states a representation contract without assuming any storage implementation meets it.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetIsomorphism: One global blank renaming and its inverse preserve the default graph and every named pair in both directions. Inverse laws cover all occurring blanks, including blank graph-name keys; IRIs and literals are fixed by the pointwise maps. No independent per-graph renaming is allowed.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetIsomorphism.default_isomorp: A dataset isomorphism induces the existing graph isomorphism on the two default graphs, using the same global blank maps.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetIsomorphism.inverse_default: The inverse global blank map takes the target default graph back to the original default graph.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetIsomorphism.symm: Reverse a dataset isomorphism by swapping its two blank maps. Named-pair preservation and the default-graph equation hold in the reverse direction.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetIsomorphism.maps_blank: Every occurring source blank maps to an occurring target blank, including occurrences only in empty graph-name keys.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetIsomorphism.injective_on_bl: The global map cannot identify two distinct blanks that occur in the source dataset, regardless of which components contain them.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetIsomorphism.refl: Every dataset is isomorphic to itself through the identity blank maps.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetIsomorphism.trans: Compose dataset isomorphisms into another dataset isomorphism. Occurrence preservation supplies the inverse laws across the intermediate dataset.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetIsomorphism.named_iff: For a name and graph whose blanks lie in the source dataset, named-pair membership is equivalent to membership of its globally renamed pair in the target. The domain premise matches the scope of the source bijection.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetIsomorphism.named_isomorphi: Each present named graph is graph-isomorphic to its corresponding globally renamed graph in the target dataset. This uses the same maps as every other component.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetIsomorphism.default_equival: Dataset-isomorphic structures have simply logically equivalent default graphs, by the previously proved semantic invariance of graph isomorphism.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetIsomorphism.named_equivalen: Each named graph of a dataset is simply logically equivalent to its corresponding graph under a dataset isomorphism. This is a component-graph consequence, not a definition of dataset entailment.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetSharingExample.defaultFor: The example default graph has one triple: an IRI subject and predicate point to the selected blank identity.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetSharingExample.namedFor: The example named graph has one triple: the selected blank subject points through an IRI predicate to an IRI object.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetSharingExample.dataset: Keep the named graph fixed at blank false, while choosing which blank appears in the default graph. One IRI names the fixed graph; the whole example uses one abstract IRI and no literals.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetSharingExample.default_map: Renaming the example default graph changes exactly its selected blank identity.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetSharingExample.named_map: Renaming the example named graph changes exactly its selected blank identity.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetSharingExample.default_inje: The example default graphs are equal only if their selected blank identities are equal.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetSharingExample.named_inject: The example named graphs are equal only if their selected blank identities are equal.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetSharingExample.default_isom: Swapping the two Boolean blank identities gives a graph isomorphism between the example default graphs considered on their own.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetSharingExample.defaults_equ: The two example default graphs are simply logically equivalent, by the existing graph-isomorphism theorem.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetSharingExample.named_graphs: The example replacement changes no named graph or graph-name key at all.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetSharingExample.no_dataset_i: No global dataset isomorphism can relate the two examples: the default graph forces false to map to true, while the fixed named graph forces false to map to false. Equivalent default replacement can therefore disrupt cross-graph sharing.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetSharingExample.empty_blank_: The blank used only as the name of an empty named graph counts as an occurring dataset blank.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetSharingExample.empty_named_: A present empty named graph cannot disappear under dataset isomorphism; the target must preserve every named pair.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetIsomorphism.surjective_on_b: Every occurring target blank has an occurring source preimage under the same global map. Together with occurrence preservation and injectivity, this explicitly establishes the required bijection on dataset blanks.
declarations.RDF11.Dataset.ofPairs: Construct a dataset lookup from an arbitrary, possibly infinite set of name/graph pairs and a proof of name uniqueness. Classical choice selects each uniquely associated graph; this is a mathematical representation equivalence, not an executable ingestion procedure.
declarations.RDF11.Dataset.ofPairs_named_iff: The partial lookup constructed from unique-name pairs contains exactly the source pairs. Combined with name_unique, this proves that the functional representation neither loses nor adds permitted named-graph associations.
declarations.RDF11.Graph.generalize_empty: Embedding the empty ordinary RDF graph into generalized syntax gives the empty generalized graph.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetRegime: An explicit candidate truth relation for datasets over an arbitrary model type, which may encode a modal structure. Inhabiting this interface does not certify an admissible RDF semantic extension or impose the source default-content recommendation.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetRegime.Entails: Within the chosen regime, every model satisfying the first dataset also satisfies the second. The regime must be stated; this is not an unqualified RDF dataset entailment definition.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetRegime.EntailsUnder: Entailment for a chosen dataset truth relation, considering only models satisfying the stated model-class condition.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetRegime.entails_refl: Every dataset entails itself within any one fixed regime.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetRegime.entails_trans: Entailment composes within a fixed dataset regime.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetRegime.restrict_entailment: An entailment valid in all models remains valid when only a selected class of those models is considered, without changing dataset truth.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetRegime.stronger_models_pres: Further restricting the model class preserves entailments when the dataset truth relation stays fixed.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetRegime.restricted: Build a regime whose models are the selected models of an existing regime. The truth relation is inherited unchanged.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetRegime.restricted_entails_i: Using a subtype of selected models is equivalent to placing the same model-class premise in the entailment quantifier.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetRegime.IncludesDefault: The explicitly adopted default-content condition: dataset truth implies truth of its default graph in a designated graph interpretation. The source condition is a conditional SHOULD recommendation; this predicate is not imposed on every regime.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetRegime.EntailsGraph: A dataset has a graph consequence under the stated regime and designated graph interpretations if every model of that dataset makes the graph true.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetRegime.default_content: A regime satisfying the adopted default-content condition makes each dataset imply its own default graph.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetRegime.default_graph_conseq: Under the adopted default-content condition, every simple consequence of the default graph is a consequence of the dataset policy. This composes with the existing simple-entailment definition.

The same consequence transfer works for an RDF/RDFS or other graph model class when every designated interpretation satisfies that class condition. The graph-regime and policy assumptions remain explicit.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetRegime.graph_consequence_co: A graph consequence of a dataset can be followed by a simple graph entailment to obtain another graph consequence under the same policy.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetRegime.restriction_includes: Restricting models while keeping dataset truth fixed preserves an already adopted default-content condition.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetRegime.simpleDefault: One chosen policy: dataset truth is exactly truth of its default graph. Its models range over all simple interpretations in the declared universe; named graphs supply no additional content in this example policy.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetRegime.simpleDefault_includ: The default-only example satisfies the adopted default-content recommendation.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetRegime.simpleDefault_entail: Entailment in the default-only policy is exactly simple entailment between the two default graphs, with the same universe scope.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetRegime.simpleDefault_isomor: The default-only policy preserves truth under dataset isomorphism by reusing the existing default-graph isomorphism theorem. No such invariance is asserted for an arbitrary chosen regime.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetModelMap: An explicit map from models of a new chosen regime to models of an old regime that preserves and reflects dataset truth for every dataset.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetModelMap.preserves_entailme: A truth-preserving model map transfers old-regime entailments to the new regime. Mere dataset-dependent strengthening of truth would not supply this premise.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetPolicyExample.nameRequired: An illustrative policy adds the presence of a fixed IRI graph name to default-only truth. It changes truth depending on the dataset, rather than merely restricting models with truth unchanged. The IRI key avoids dependence on a chosen ambient blank identity.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetPolicyExample.nameRequired_: The name-presence policy still implies default-graph truth, so it satisfies the adopted default-content condition.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetPolicyExample.default_only_: Under default-only truth, the dataset containing an empty named graph entails the dataset with no named graphs, because the latter has an empty default graph.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetPolicyExample.nameRequired_: Requiring the name to be present invalidates that entailment: a concrete model satisfies the dataset with the empty named graph, while no model of this policy satisfies the dataset lacking the name. Default-content preservation alone does not preserve all old dataset entailments.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetNameExample.graph: A singleton ground graph uses one selected IRI as subject, predicate and object. It is generic over arbitrary IRI, literal and blank domains, including the full RDF domains.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetNameExample.dataset: For any selected IRI, make the singleton graph both the default graph and the graph paired with that IRI; all other names are absent. The ambient IRI/literal/blank domains remain arbitrary.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetNameExample.Carrier: The example resource universe contains an injectively tagged object for every graph over the supplied full syntactic domains, plus a distinct non-graph object. It is a chosen witness carrier, not a mandated universe.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetNameExample.graphObject: Embed each graph over the arbitrary supplied domains as a distinct tagged resource object. This graph-object representation is a choice for the witness.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetNameExample.graphObject_inj: The chosen graph-object embedding is injective for arbitrary supplied IRI, literal and blank domains.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetNameExample.nameValue: Select whether the globally assigned IRI referent is the object for the selected singleton graph or a distinct non-graph object.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetNameExample.interpretation: A simple interpretation over arbitrary full IRI/literal domains: IS assigns every IRI a resource/property, including unused names; IL is an everywhere-undefined partial map on the entire literal type. Full relation extensions make the ground witness true. This is not an RDF/RDFS interpretation construction.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetNameExample.named_pair: The selected IRI is paired with its singleton graph in the chosen dataset, independently of either interpretation.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetNameExample.graph_satisfied: For any selected IRI and arbitrary syntactic domains, its singleton graph is true in both full-domain simple interpretations. No blank occurs in the graph, though the ambient blank type is unrestricted.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetNameExample.all_components_: Every component graph of the chosen dataset is true in either full-domain simple interpretation. A constant temporary assignment is restricted by the existing satisfaction theorem to the blanks actually occurring in the graph.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetNameExample.name_can_denote: For any selected IRI, one full-domain simple interpretation maps that IRI to the explicitly embedded object for its paired graph.
For the same selected IRI, the other full-domain simple interpretation maps it to the distinct non-graph object.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetNameExample.pairing_and_com: For arbitrary IRI, literal and blank domains, the same selected named pair and true graph admit identity or nonidentity between the name referent and its paired graph object. IS covers every IRI and IL is a permitted partial map on all literals. Stronger semantic regimes and additional graph conditions remain separate.
declarations.RDF11.Dataset.namedGraphOrEmpty: For the illustrative matching-name comparison, use the graph at a name when present and the empty graph when absent. This deliberately forgets the distinction between a present empty graph and a missing key.
declarations.RDF11.Dataset.namedGraphOrEmpty_of_prese: The comparison lookup returns exactly the graph paired with a present name.
declarations.RDF11.Dataset.namedGraphOrEmpty_of_absen: The comparison lookup substitutes an empty graph at a missing name, following the source illustration.
declarations.RDF11.Dataset.emptyNamed_graphAt: Every lookup in a dataset containing only one empty named graph yields an empty graph under the comparison lookup.
declarations.RDF11.NamedGraphComparison: Require a chosen graph consequence relation at every exact matching syntactic graph-name key, filling missing graphs with empty graphs. This compares named components independently, omits the default, and supplies no common witness across graphs or alignment of renamed keys. It is a possible necessary comparison condition, not complete dataset semantics.
declarations.RDF11.namedGraphComparison_refl: If the chosen graph relation is reflexive, its matching-name comparison is reflexive too.
declarations.RDF11.namedGraphComparison_trans: If graph consequences compose, the corresponding matching-name comparisons compose at each fixed key.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleNamedGraphComparison: Specialize the optional matching-name condition to simple graph entailment. Keys are compared by syntactic identity; no invariance under blank graph-name renaming is asserted.
declarations.RDF11.empty_named_matches_absent: The present-empty and absent-name datasets satisfy this simple matching-name condition in both directions, because missing names are filled with empty graphs.
declarations.RDF11.matching_graphs_need_not_be_isomor: Mutual matching-name graph consequences do not guarantee dataset isomorphism: the presence of an empty named graph is lost by the comparison, while the earlier structural theorem proves the datasets non-isomorphic.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetIsomorphism.iri_name_presen: A dataset isomorphism preserves whether a fixed IRI graph name is present, including when its graph is empty. The IRI itself is fixed by the global blank renaming.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetPolicyExample.nameRequired_: The fixed-IRI presence policy respects dataset isomorphism: both default truth and presence of that IRI key are invariant. Its changed entailments therefore do not depend on naming a particular ambient blank identity.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetRegime.defaultUnder: The chosen default-only policy restricted to all interpretations satisfying an explicit graph-regime condition, such as the existing RDF or RDFS conditions. This definition does not prove that the model class is inhabited.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetRegime.defaultUnder_entails: Entailment in the selected default-only policy is exactly the existing graph-regime entailment between defaults. This provides an exact bridge to RDF/RDFS graph entailment when their conditions are supplied.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetRegime.defaultUnder_include: The chosen default-only policy over any selected graph regime satisfies the adopted default-content condition.
declarations.RDF11.DatasetRegime.defaultUnder_isomorp: The selected graph-regime default-only policy preserves truth under dataset isomorphism, using the same graph-isomorphism result without requiring new model-existence assumptions.
declarations.RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.Parameters: Sufficient assumptions for this RDF model family: the literal and vocabulary langString names agree, language strings and strings are recognized, and rdf:type, rdf:Property and rdf:List are not recognized datatypes. The three exclusions are construction hypotheses, not specification requirements or necessary consistency conditions.
declarations.RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.Carrier: The model universe contains an injective copy of every external value, a separate name object for each supplied IRI, and one unnamed object. ULift permits the carrier universe required by the existing entailment definition.
declarations.RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.embed: Place an external value into the value part of the model universe, preserving its identity.
declarations.RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.name: Place an IRI into the separate name part of the model universe. This is one model choice; RDF does not require every IRI to denote a distinct resource.
declarations.RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.unnamed: A spare resource used for literals whose datatype is not recognized; this does not assign them a prescribed datatype meaning.
declarations.RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.lift: Embed the previously constructed D-model universe into this larger RDF universe. Existing literal values retain their identity; the old spare resource becomes the new spare resource.
declarations.RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.realization: Realize every external value injectively in the RDF carrier. Realizing all values is a choice of this witness family, not a new requirement that every RDF model contain values outside recognized spaces.
declarations.RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.iriValue: Every recognized datatype IRI denotes its embedded fixed external datatype, including langString. Other IRIs have separate name objects. Recognized aliases of one datatype co-denote.
declarations.RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.typeExtension: Datatype-object columns retain their actual identity-indexed spaces, including the language-pair exception and aliases. Named columns are universal in this witness family. The extra unnamed carrier resource now has an empty column, providing an empty class in the proved RDFS extension; this changes a witness choice, not the semantic conditions.
declarations.RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.interpretatio: Construct a simple interpretation over every supplied IRI and literal. All carrier elements are resources and properties; rdf:type uses the fixed typeExtension and every other property uses the supplied arbitrary relation R. Literal denotations reuse the earlier D-model construction. conditions separately proves that this is an RDF interpretation under Parameters; no RDFS claim is made.
declarations.RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.iriValue_unre: An IRI outside the recognized datatype set maps to its separate name object in this construction.
declarations.RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.relates_iff: Connect the existing typed IEXT relation to this constructor: rdf:type uses its fixed extension, while a different property uses exactly the supplied relation R.
declarations.RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.literalValue_: Transport an already proved literal-value fact from the D-model into the larger RDF carrier, preserving both literal denotation and external value identity.
declarations.RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.datatypes: Every member of this construction family satisfies the existing DConditions, by transporting the earlier D-model proof. This statement alone does not assert the additional RDF conditions.
declarations.RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.datatype_colu: For each recognized datatype IRI, the chosen rdf:type column is exactly its realized datatype value space, including langString and any alias of that datatype.
declarations.RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.named_column: An unrecognized IRI denotes a name object whose rdf:type column contains every resource in this chosen model family. This supplies the property and list columns needed by the RDF axioms.
declarations.RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.conditions: Verify all existing RDFConditions at once: D semantics, mandatory recognition, property typing, full value realization, exact datatype columns and every RDF axiom, including the infinite container family. The sufficient Parameters hypotheses remain explicit.
declarations.RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.model: Package the constructed realization and the proof of RDFConditions into the existing RDFModel predicate. This is an actual existence witness, not an assumed model-class field.
declarations.RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.empty_satisfi: Exhibit a full RDF interpretation satisfying the empty graph under the construction hypotheses. The witness uses empty extensions for every non-rdf:type property.
declarations.RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.base_paramete: Prove that recognizing exactly rdf:langString and xsd:string meets the construction hypotheses, using vocabulary distinctness and the explicit agreement of the langString name. Prescribed datatype meanings remain external parameters.
declarations.RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.base_empty_sa: Exhibit a carrier and RDF model of the empty graph for the base recognition set. Concrete RDF syntax and built-in datatype correspondence still need separate validation.
declarations.RDF11.RDFModelConstruction.non_type_trip: For an unrecognized predicate distinct from rdf:type, a triple of IRIs is true in this model exactly when the chosen relation R contains the three corresponding denotations.

Give two full RDF models for the same compatible parameters: one satisfies the chosen all-IRI triple and the other falsifies it. Thus the triple is satisfiable but is not RDF-entailed by the empty graph. Its predicate must be unrecognized and different from rdf:type; this does not establish RDFS independence.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.rdf_property_: If rdf:Property is recognized as a datatype, every RDF model forces its value space to contain a value: the mandatory rdf:type rdf:type rdf:Property triple supplies a member. This is a derived compatibility constraint on external datatype parameters.
declarations.RDF11.rdf_unsatisfiable_of_empty_propert: An external theory recognizing rdf:Property with an empty value space has no RDF model, so every graph is RDF-unsatisfiable for those parameters. This does not claim that the prescribed standard datatypes have that defect.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.rdfs_language: In an RDFS interpretation, each language-pair value has an actual tagged-literal representative. The proof combines full RDF value-space realization, the RDFS literal-image equality, and injectivity of value realization; the tag value is lowercased by the existing ASCII rule.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.rdfsModel_lan: Obtain the same tagged-literal coverage requirement from the packaged RDFSModel predicate by unpacking its realization and semantic conditions.
declarations.RDF11.rdfs_unsatisfiable_of_missing_lang: If an abstract literal domain omits a representative of a permitted language-string value, no RDFS interpretation over those parameters exists. This exposes an incomplete domain interface, not an inconsistency in the RDF specification.
declarations.RDF11.rdf_unsatisfiable_implies_rdfs_uns: Every RDFS model is already an RDF model with the same recognized datatypes. Consequently, the absence of RDF models implies the absence of RDFS models for the same graph.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeTheory.datatypeSpace: Choose the actual value space by datatype identity: the identified language datatype has the normalized string/tag pair space, and every other datatype has its L2V range. Using identities ensures that aliases of one datatype share its space.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeTheory.recognizedSpace_lan: The canonical langString IRI selects exactly the language-pair value space.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeTheory.recognizedSpace_ide: IRIs identifying the same datatype select the same value space. This includes aliases of the exceptional language datatype without assuming IRI identification is injective.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeTheory.l2v_in_datatypeSpac: A successful L2V evaluation produces a member of the actual datatype space. Its datatype cannot be the exceptional language datatype, whose L2V evaluation is nowhere defined.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeTheory.language_noL2V: Encode the absent language-datatype L2V operation as an everywhere-undefined partial evaluator. Its actual value space is the separate pair space; this field does not make that datatype empty-valued.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeTheory.language_alias_illT: An ordinary literal using a recognized noncanonical alias of langString has no L2V value and is ill-typed. This is a derived edge-case reading; it does not apply to canonical tagged literals, and expert mapping review remains pending.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.DConditions.l: When langString is recognized, its IRI denotes the fixed language datatype represented by T.identified, through the shared value realization. This records the section 7 prose obligation omitted by the earlier table-only encoding.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.recognized_da: Every recognized datatype IRI denotes its fixed external datatype, including langString. The proof combines the newly retained prose obligation with the ordinary table row.
Two recognized IRIs identifying the same datatype have the same denotation in every D-interpretation. This preserves permitted aliases without imposing global injectivity of datatype identification.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.LanguageCove: Every value in the supplied language-string value space has an actual tagged literal whose lexical text and ASCII-lowercased tag denote that value. This is a condition on the literal interface, not merely on the supply of semantic values.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.SchemaSymbol: A constructor-local label for the RDF/RDFS vocabulary symbols other than rdf:langString and xsd:string. It is used to state sufficient recognition exclusions, not a new specification category.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.Parameters: Sufficient assumptions for this RDFS model family: aligned langString names, recognition of language strings and strings, non-recognition of the other schema symbols, and actual language-literal coverage. The exclusions are constructor choices, not requirements on every RDFS model.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.Parameters.t: The chosen RDFS constructor assumptions imply the assumptions needed by the existing RDF model construction. This lets the RDFS proof reuse all RDF and datatype conditions.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.schemaName: The fresh name-object assigned by the constructor to a vocabulary symbol. Recognized datatype IRIs instead denote their embedded datatype identities; the name-object is their denotation only when the recognition exclusion applies.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.schemaName_e: Two constructor name-objects for vocabulary symbols are equal exactly when the symbols are equal. This follows from distinct vocabulary IRIs and the disjoint carrier constructors.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.NameObject: A resource belongs to the name-object part of the constructed carrier when it was made with name from an IRI. These objects have universal class extensions in this family; embedded datatype objects retain their exact datatype spaces.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.subclass: The chosen subclass relation is inclusion of the existing rdf:type class columns: every member of the first class is a member of the second. This is a model choice, not an equivalence required of every RDFS interpretation.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.subproperty: The chosen subproperty relation contains equality, every property pointing to rdfs:member, and rdfs:isDefinedBy pointing to rdfs:seeAlso. The target relations member and seeAlso are universal in this family.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.relation: Choose extensions for the schema properties: existing rdf:type columns, class-column inclusion, the chosen subproperty relation, and domain/range targets restricted to name-objects. member and seeAlso relate every pair. Q controls remaining properties and cannot override these schema roles.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.interpretati: Reuse the full-domain RDF interpretation with the chosen schema relations. All supplied IRIs and literals retain denotation functions. The subsequent conditions theorem proves that this interpretation also meets every RDFS condition under Parameters.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.relates_iff: The typed property-extension relation of the constructed interpretation agrees with the chosen relation. The outer RDF dispatch for rdf:type and the inner RDFS dispatch use the same type columns.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.schema_denot: Under the constructor exclusions, a schema symbol denotes its separate name-object, so the proof can calculate its property and class extensions explicitly.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.relates_subc: In this family, applying the denotation of rdfs:subClassOf is exactly inclusion of the existing class columns.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.relates_subp: In this family, applying the denotation of rdfs:subPropertyOf is exactly the selected reflexive relation with member and seeAlso targets.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.relates_doma: In this family, every property has every name-object as a domain class. Each such class extension is universal, so the domain condition is respected. Recognized datatype-object columns are not made universal.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.relates_rang: In this family, every property has every name-object as a range class. Each such class extension is universal, so the range condition is respected. Recognized datatype-object columns are not made universal.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.icext_iff: The class extension defined through rdf:type is exactly the type column already supplied by the RDF construction. This keeps recognized datatype value spaces unchanged.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.named_column: Each schema symbol excluded from recognition has a universal class extension in this witness family. This does not include the recognized langString or string datatype symbols.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.all_classes: Every resource is a class in this witness family. Having every resource in IC does not require every class extension to be universal: datatype classes retain their prescribed member sets.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.all_literal_: Every resource belongs to LV in this witness family. The specification does not equate LV with the image of IL or the supplied external Value domain. This construction is a permitted choice under the current interfaces, not a claim about all RDFS models.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.subproperty_: The explicitly selected subproperty relation is transitive. Vocabulary distinctness rules out spurious paths between member, seeAlso and isDefinedBy.
The selected subproperty pairs respect inclusion of property extensions: identity preserves a relation, and the other pairs have universal member or seeAlso extensions as targets.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.domain_targe: Every target in the existing finite list of RDFS domain axioms is a schema symbol excluded from datatype recognition by the constructor hypotheses.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.range_target: Every target in the existing finite list of RDFS range axioms is a schema symbol excluded from datatype recognition by the constructor hypotheses.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.hierarchy_ca: The existing finite hierarchy axiom list consists of subclass statements with schema targets and the isDefinedBy-to-seeAlso subproperty statement. This proof reuses the registered axiom list.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.axioms: The constructed interpretation satisfies every RDFS axiomatic triple, including all positive container indices. The proof combines the actual domain, range and hierarchy lists with the complete container family.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.language_ext: The langString class extension equals the denotations of actual tagged literals. The forward direction uses the explicit literal-coverage hypothesis; the reverse uses the existing RDF literal-typing proof.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.conditions: Every existing RDFS semantic condition holds for the constructed interpretation. The proof reuses RDF conditions, proves exact language-literal coverage, and checks domain/range, hierarchy, container, datatype and full axiom obligations. No condition is dropped.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.model: Package the constructed value realization and the proof of all RDFS conditions into an inhabitant of the existing RDFSModel definition.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.base_paramet: For D containing exactly langString and string, vocabulary distinctness discharges the constructor recognition exclusions. Agreement of names and coverage by actual tagged literals remain explicit hypotheses.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.empty_satisf: Under Parameters, exhibit a carrier and an actual RDFS model satisfying the empty graph. This proves model-class inhabitation, not satisfiability of arbitrary graphs.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.base_empty_s: With base datatype recognition, aligned langString names and language-literal coverage, exhibit an RDFS model satisfying the empty graph.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.base_model_e: With base datatype recognition and aligned langString names, an RDFS model exists in the current parameterized interfaces exactly when every language value has an actual tagged-literal representative. Necessity reuses the earlier coverage theorem; sufficiency uses the new construction. This is not a criterion for arbitrary-graph consistency or a certification of concrete built-in datatypes.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.iri_literal_: In the constructed family, any IRI subject can have rdf:type rdfs:Literal, since the Literal class column is universal. This is a witness choice, not a consequence true of every IRI in every RDFS model.

Exhibit an RDFS model satisfying a rdf:type rdfs:Literal with IRI subject a, under the constructor assumptions. This proves the consistency example in §9.1, not every part of the syntax-versus-value distinction.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.overlapping_: Exhibit an RDFS model in which every resource is simultaneously a property, a class and a literal value. This establishes that the semantic roles need not be disjoint; fixed datatype value spaces still remain distinct as specified by the parameters.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.distinct_coe: In this family, rdfs:Class and rdfs:Resource have distinct denotations but identical class extensions. This gives an explicit witness that equality of extensions does not force identity of classes.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.class_self_m: The constructed interpretation makes rdfs:Class a member of its own class extension. This instance connects the permitted self-membership observation to the same RDFS model proof.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.property_sel: The constructed interpretation satisfies rdfs:member rdfs:member rdfs:member. This exhibits a property applying to itself while all RDFS conditions hold.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.value_triple: An rdf:value triple between the chosen schema-name resources holds exactly when the freely supplied Q relation holds. rdf:value is only an example property; its property typing and Resource domain/range axioms are already satisfied. It is not a literal-value evaluation operation.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.no_class_mem: Construct two RDFS countermodels: an rdf:value assertion on a class need not hold of an individual typed member, and an assertion on that member need not hold of the class. The class and member are distinct selected schema-name resources. This refutes two particular entailments; additional premises may imply transfer.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.FreeProperty: A constructor-local test that excludes the schema relations handled specially by the model. A property passing this test has extension supplied by Q. Its RDF/RDFS axioms still hold; this is not a new W3C vocabulary category.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.relates_free: For an unrecognized designated property outside the fixed schema dispatch, the model relation equals Q on every pair of resources. This shared calculation supports reification and container countermodels.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.free_iri_tri: A triple between selected name-object resources with a free predicate is true exactly when Q contains the corresponding pair. Explicit recognition and dispatch hypotheses keep built-in constraints intact.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.schema_type_: Any IRI subject is typed by a selected unrecognized schema class in this witness family, since that class column is universal. It is a property of the constructed family, not every RDFS model.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.free_blank_t: A free-predicate triple with a blank subject and selected IRI object is true exactly when the blank has a denotation related by Q to that object. The subject remains existential; the theorem does not fix its identity.
declarations.RDF11.Triple.reification: Build the four ordinary RDF triples assigning Statement type and subject, predicate and object components to a resource. This describes components without asserting the described triple. Identification with a concrete triple token is not supplied by this syntax definition.
declarations.RDF11.ReificationScopeReview.blank_prope: If a premise graph has a blank-subject property triple, it simply entails the same property/object triple with any conclusion blank label. The conclusion has its own existential assignment and can reuse the premise witness. The blank types may differ.
declarations.RDF11.ReificationScopeReview.printedPrem: The nine ordinary triples printed in Appendix D.1 paragraph 12: two four-triple reifications with identical components and one property assertion on the first root. Bool false and true represent the two printed blank labels.
declarations.RDF11.ReificationScopeReview.printed_con: The printed nine-triple premise simply entails the standalone property triple on the second blank label. The conclusion reuses the first root’s property witness under independent existential scope. This checked positive result supports an open source question, not a declared erratum or acceptance of the printed non-entailment.
declarations.RDF11.ReificationExamples.valueTriple: An ordinary IRI-only triple using rdf:value as the example assertion predicate, with subject and object selected from the designated vocabulary. This is a witness choice, not an operation evaluating literal values.
declarations.RDF11.ReificationExamples.reification_tr: In the constructed RDFS family, the four describing triples are true when Q contains the three component edges; the Statement typing comes from the existing class-column proof. Both reification countermodels and the metadata example reuse this proof.
declarations.RDF11.ReificationExamples.reification_no: An actual RDFS countermodel makes the four reification triples true while leaving the described rdf:value assertion false. This refutes a general inference pattern for the selected witness family, not every possible triple or every set of additional premises.
declarations.RDF11.ReificationExamples.assertion_not_: An actual RDFS countermodel satisfies the example assertion but has no rdf:subject edges at all. No existential root can therefore satisfy its complete reification. This is stronger than merely falsifying one chosen named root.
declarations.RDF11.ReificationExamples.same_component: Two distinct named resources can describe identical triple components while metadata holds on only the first. The countermodel refutes transfer to the second. It does not impose a unique-name assumption on all interpretations and does not prove the printed existential blank-node example.
declarations.RDF11.ContainerExamples.twoMemberBag: The ordinary source-shaped Bag premise: one blank root, Bag typing, and first and second indexed members. The list is interpreted as a set of triples. Index zero in the vocabulary denotes rdf:_1.
declarations.RDF11.ContainerExamples.twoPositions: The printed permutation conclusion contains only two indexed membership triples on one blank root. No container typing is silently added to the conclusion.
declarations.RDF11.ContainerExamples.gappedSequence: The ordinary source-shaped sequence premise: one blank root, Seq typing, and members at rdf:_1 and rdf:_3, without an rdf:_2 assertion.
declarations.RDF11.ContainerExamples.bag_permutation_: Construct an RDFS model of the two-member Bag where _1 relates only to the first selected value and _2 only to the second. Distinct values prevent any existential root from witnessing the swapped conclusion. The result refutes automatic permutation, not explicit assertions of both orders.
declarations.RDF11.ContainerExamples.second_position_: Construct an RDFS model of the gapped sequence with an entirely empty rdf:_2 extension. No assignment to either conclusion blank can make the missing-index triple true; distinct blank labels need not denote distinct resources.
declarations.RDF11.ContainerExamples.bag_and_sequence: Exhibit an RDFS model typing the same IRI-named resource as both Bag and Seq under the constructor assumptions. This establishes that those two container types need not be disjoint.
declarations.RDF11.ContainerExamples.no_container_mem: Construct countermodels in both directions between a Bag and one identified indexed member: an rdf:value assertion on one need not hold of the other. The chosen premises do not transfer it; additional axioms or properties asserted of every member are separate questions.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration.no_enumeration_of_nat_: If a set contains a distinct member for every natural number, no finite list can enumerate the entire set. The proof compares one more distinct indexed member than a proposed list can hold. This applies to sets of triples, pairs or resources; it does not make every RDF graph finite.
declarations.RDF11.RDFVocabulary.container_injective: Different natural-number indices give different abstract container-property IRI names. This follows from vocabulary-name distinctness, not from distinct denotations of those names.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.ISGraph: The set of pairs consisting of an IRI and its IS denotation, which may lie in IR or IP in a simple interpretation. This is the mathematical graph of a function, not an RDF graph or a stored list.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.ISGraph_not_f: An infinite distinct family of IRI names makes the graph of IS impossible to enumerate finitely. Names remain distinct as first components even if every denotation is the same resource.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.vocabulary_IS: The indexed container-property names supply the distinct input family needed to prove that the graph of IS has no finite enumeration.
declarations.RDF11.one_resource_infinite_name_mapping: A simple interpretation can have exactly one resource while its IS mapping has infinitely many name/denotation pairs. Its resource domain has a finite enumeration and its name-mapping graph does not. This is a full-domain simple witness, not an RDF/RDFS model or a finite-vocabulary pre-interpretation.
declarations.RDF11.ContainerInfinitude.bagType: The ordinary triple typing a chosen IRI-named root as an rdf:Bag. The witness reuses the rdfs:Resource IRI as a root; overlap of RDF semantic roles is permitted.
declarations.RDF11.ContainerInfinitude.indexedTriple: At natural-number index n, the root has an rdf:_(n+1) edge whose object is that indexed property IRI. Using a property name as an object is permitted by ordinary RDF syntax.
declarations.RDF11.ContainerInfinitude.allIndexed: The ordinary set-valued RDF graph containing the root Bag typing and all natural-number-indexed membership triples. No finite cutoff is imposed.
declarations.RDF11.ContainerInfinitude.finitePrefix: A finite ordinary graph containing the Bag typing and the indexed edges below k. Set construction discards repetition and order.
declarations.RDF11.ContainerInfinitude.prefixEnumerat: A finite list with membership and uniqueness proofs enumerates the displayed prefix. The implementation uses the existing deduplicating list-to-enumeration construction.
declarations.RDF11.ContainerInfinitude.prefix_subset: Every displayed finite prefix is a subgraph of the graph containing all indexed edges.
declarations.RDF11.ContainerInfinitude.prefix_next: The next prefix is exactly the union of the current prefix with the next indexed triple. This equality alone does not state proper inclusion or exact cardinality.
declarations.RDF11.ContainerInfinitude.allIndexed_gro: The infinite ordinary graph contains no blank nodes; its blank-node type is empty.
declarations.RDF11.ContainerInfinitude.indexed_genera: Equal generalized indexed triples must have equal predicates, hence equal vocabulary indices. Generalizing the triples does not collapse the infinite family.
declarations.RDF11.ContainerInfinitude.allIndexed_not: No finite certified enumeration contains exactly the triples of this generalized ordinary graph, because the graph includes a distinct triple for every natural number.
declarations.RDF11.ContainerInfinitude.interpretation: Reuse the previously verified RDFS interpretation constructor with every free property edge chosen true. This is one witness interpretation; these universal relations are not conditions imposed on all models.
declarations.RDF11.ContainerInfinitude.allIndexed_tru: Under the sufficient constructor hypotheses, the chosen RDFS interpretation makes the Bag typing and every indexed triple true. The graph is ground, so no blank-node witnesses are needed.
declarations.RDF11.ContainerInfinitude.allIndexed_sat: Under the explicit constructor hypotheses, an RDFS model satisfies the infinite graph. This proves existence for this graph, not for arbitrary graphs.
declarations.RDF11.ContainerInfinitude.prefixes_exten: One RDFS model satisfies every displayed finite prefix and its extension by the next indexed edge. Each prefix has a certified finite enumeration. This is a particular family, not arbitrary-graph membership-extension consistency.
declarations.RDF11.ContainerInfinitude.infinite_membe: An RDFS model satisfies the infinite graph and gives a Bag root distinct indexed member denotations. Each indexed edge also gives an rdfs:member edge through the existing subproperty conditions. Distinct denotations are chosen in this model; other models may identify them.
declarations.RDF11.ContainerInfinitude.nonfinite_memb: The chosen Bag has a generic rdfs:member extension with no finite enumeration. The proof reuses the distinct-member family and the general finite-enumeration impossibility theorem, under the same constructor hypotheses.
declarations.RDF11.vocabulary_domain_derivable: A domain axiom in the existing RDFS vocabulary table, together with a property edge, derives the required subject type by rdfs2. All triples share the same blank domain.
declarations.RDF11.vocabulary_range_derivable: A range axiom in the existing RDFS vocabulary table, together with a property edge, derives the required object type by rdfs3. This is a derivation from existing axioms, not a new model assumption.
declarations.RDF11.collection_first_subject_derivable: Every subject of an rdf:first edge can be derived to have type rdf:List, using the existing domain axiom.
declarations.RDF11.collection_rest_typing_derivable: Both the subject and object of every rdf:rest edge can be derived to have type rdf:List. This says nothing about whether they form a well-formed terminating chain.
declarations.RDF11.collection_first_subject_entailmen: Every RDFS interpretation satisfying the premise graph also satisfies the List typing of the indicated first-edge subject. The proof reuses derivation soundness.
declarations.RDF11.collection_rest_typing_entailment: Every RDFS model of the premise satisfies the two List typing triples for the indicated rest edge, with one shared assignment. No construction-specific model hypotheses are needed.
declarations.RDF11.collection_nil_typing_derivable: The RDF axiom rdf:nil rdf:type rdf:List is derivable regardless of the premise graph. This does not require nil to lack outgoing edges.
declarations.RDF11.Collections.cell: The ordinary two-triple description connecting one root to an item by rdf:first and to a tail by rdf:rest. It adds no type triple and makes no claim that all collection graphs have this shape.
declarations.RDF11.Collections.twoItemChain: The source example as a set of four ordinary triples on two existential blanks: first item, rest link to the second cell, second item, and rest link to nil. The same constructor expresses the reversed conclusion with exchanged items.
declarations.RDF11.Collections.branchingCell: The printed four-triple branching description: one existential root has two first values and two rest values, one of the tails being nil.
declarations.RDF11.Collections.headOnly: An ordinary singleton graph stating a first value for an existential root and giving no rest information.
declarations.RDF11.CollectionExamples.permutation_not: For arbitrary distinct unrecognized item IRIs, a verified RDFS model satisfies the original two-item chain but no conclusion assignment satisfies its reversal. Both graphs have exactly the printed four edges; blanks are existential separately in each graph. The sufficient model-constructor hypotheses remain explicit.
declarations.RDF11.CollectionExamples.branching_consi: A verified RDFS model satisfies the printed branching shape with at least two distinct head denotations and at least two distinct tail denotations. All required List typing still holds; semantic class membership does not guarantee the intended chain structure.
declarations.RDF11.CollectionExamples.rest_existence_: A first-only graph is true in a verified RDFS model whose entire rest relation is empty. No existential choice of subject and object can supply a rest edge. The item can be any IRI; additional graph premises are outside this counterexample.
declarations.RDF11.CollectionExamples.nil_self_edges_: A verified RDFS model permits nil to have both a first edge and a rest edge to itself. This derived witness separates the empty-collection convention from an outgoing-edge prohibition or an acyclicity condition. Nil retains its required List type.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.unrecognized: Any IRI outside the recognized datatype set denotes its distinct name-branch object in this particular constructor. It need not be a built-in vocabulary IRI; this is not a unique-name condition on all interpretations.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.free_term_tr: A triple with a constructor-free named predicate is true precisely when its subject and object denote two resources under the same assignment and the chosen relation connects them. Their terms may include blanks, IRIs or literals.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.free_unrecog: For an arbitrary unrecognized IRI object and a constructor-free predicate, triple truth reduces to a subject denotation and the chosen edge to that name object. This extends example calculations beyond built-in vocabulary endpoints.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.unname_sound: If inverse naming selects a blank for an IRI, that blank occurs in G and its chosen Skolem name is exactly the IRI.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.liftTerm: Replace a generated IRI by the left copy of its original blank; preserve an existing conclusion blank as a right copy. Other IRIs and literals stay fixed. Separate copies prevent capture even when input blank identities overlap.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.applyLiftedTerm: Reapply original Skolem names on left-copy blanks and preserve right-copy conclusion blanks. IRIs and literals stay fixed. This extends the original naming map rather than naming every conclusion blank.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.apply_liftTerm: Lifting a conclusion term and reapplying the names returns exactly the original term, including its original blank identity.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.liftTriple: Apply inverse naming with separate blank copies to each of the three generalized triple terms.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.applyLiftedTriple: Reapply names on the original-blank copy in each triple position while retaining conclusion blanks. This operation is used in the exact lifting equation.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.apply_liftTriple: Reapplying names to a lifted generalized triple gives exactly the original triple.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.apply_liftGraph: Reapplying names to the lifted set of triples gives exactly the original graph, without finiteness or approximation.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.totalAssignment: Choose a resource for every ambient blank, using its assigned resource when present and an arbitrary existing resource otherwise. Truth already forces defined assignments for blanks occurring in the source graph.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.namedInterpretation: Retain the original IR, IP, IEXT and IL. Change IS only at generated Skolem IRIs so that each denotes the resource assigned to its original blank. This constructs a simple interpretation; it does not claim preservation of additional datatype or RDFS conditions.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.liftAssignment: Use original-source witnesses on left-copy blanks and conclusion witnesses on right-copy blanks. The copies cannot capture one another.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.denote_liftTerm: A lifted term in the original interpretation has exactly the denotation of its conclusion term in the interpretation with Skolem names assigned.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.tripleTrue_lift: Triple truth transfers through inverse naming under the combined assignment because domains and property extensions stay fixed and all three term denotations agree.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.unname_of_fresh: An IRI which is not any occurring source blank's chosen name is left outside the inverse-name map.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.named_denote_substit: For a source term whose names are fresh-name-free and whose blanks occur in G, assigning Skolem-name denotations preserves its defined denotation after substitution.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.named_satisfies_skol: Given a shared assignment making G true, the constructed interpretation satisfies sk(G). The proof transports the same subject, predicate and object witnesses; it assumes neither finite graphs nor IP contained in IR.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.entails_lift: If sk(G) simply entails H, G simply entails the graph obtained by inverse naming with separate blank copies. This holds for generalized graphs and different input blank domains. H may mention generated names and may be infinite.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.liftTerm_left_blank: Every left-copy blank introduced by inverse naming comes from an occurring blank in G. Unrelated original blank values are never introduced.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.liftGraph_left_blank: Every left-copy blank in the lifted graph belongs to the original Skolem map's occurring source domain.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.unname_predicate_of_: An ordinary conclusion entailed by a Skolemized ordinary graph cannot use a generated name as its predicate. Fixed entailed predicates occur in the premise, where original predicates were unchanged and freshness excludes those names.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.liftSubject: Inverse-name a subject while keeping it either an IRI or a blank. Existing conclusion blanks move to the separate right copy.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.liftSubject_toTerm: The ordinary subject transformation agrees with the general term transformation after embedding subjects as terms.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.liftOrdinaryTriple: Lift the subject and object while retaining the IRI predicate. Entailment supplies the proof that the predicate does not require inverse naming.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.liftOrdinaryGraph: The ordinary graph obtained by lifting every ordinary conclusion triple, with separate source and conclusion blank copies.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.generalize_liftOrdin: When the predicate is not a generated name, ordinary lifting and generalized termwise lifting give the same generalized triple.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.ordinary_lift_genera: For an entailed ordinary conclusion, the ordinary lifted graph embeds as exactly the generalized lifted graph. This supplies the missing syntax-preservation step.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.ordinary_exact_lifti: For ordinary G and H, if sk(G) simply entails H, there is an ordinary H-prime entailed by G whose original-copy blanks all occur in G and whose renamed image is exactly H. No finiteness, disjoint-input-blank or Avoids-H condition is needed. Reapplication preserves the separate conclusion-blank copy.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.total_substitution_g: The older ambient-total substitution turns every input graph into a ground graph. It is suitable for constructing sk(G), but cannot preserve unrelated conclusion blanks.
declarations.RDF11.Skolemization.total_substitution_c: If H contains a blank, no graph transformed by the older ambient-total substitution can equal H. This prevents confusing that substitution with the extension used in the exact lifting theorem.
declarations.RDF11.entailed_iri_predicate_occurs: Every fixed IRI predicate in an entailed triple occurs as a predicate in the premise. The canonical interpretation proves this even when premise and conclusion have different blank domains.
declarations.RDF11.Statements.skolemization_lifting_l: Headline alias for exact ordinary Skolem lifting. G entails an ordinary lifted conclusion, and reapplying original names while preserving conclusion blanks recovers H exactly. Separate blank copies and the occurring-source-domain guarantee are explicit; no finiteness or fresh-vocabulary restriction on H is added.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration.injective_surjective: An injective function mapping a finitely enumerated set into itself reaches every member of that set. Injectivity and closure are required only for set members, not unused ambient values. The proof would otherwise fit one extra distinct element into the same finite enumeration.
declarations.RDF11.FiniteBlankSupport: There exists an exact duplicate-free enumeration of the blank nodes occurring in the graph. This does not require a finite ambient blank type or a finite set of triples; a ground graph may still have infinitely many triples.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.blankList: Collect the blank terms in the subject, predicate and object of a generalized triple. This local list may repeat a blank; it is only an intermediate enumeration input, not a graph representation.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.mem_blankList: A blank is in the collected list exactly when it occurs in the triple under the existing syntactic occurrence definition.
declarations.RDF11.finite_blank_support_of_finite_gra: A finite graph has finitely many occurring blanks. Collect blanks from its certified triple enumeration, remove repetitions with the existing enumeration constructor, and prove exact membership.
declarations.RDF11.Term.substitute_blank_origin: A blank in a substituted term must come from an original blank whose resolved replacement is exactly that output blank. Fixed IRIs and literals cannot introduce a blank.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedGraph.substitute_blank_: Every blank occurring after graph substitution comes from an occurring source blank mapped to that blank. The statement preserves one substitution across every triple position.
declarations.RDF11.ProperSubstitution.then: Once a substitution replaces an occurring blank by a name or identifies distinct occurring blanks, a later substitution cannot undo that properness. Names stay fixed and equal replacement terms stay equal.
declarations.RDF11.finite_blank_self_substitution_not: A substitution that leaves a graph unchanged cannot be proper when the occurring blank set is finite. Every output blank has a predecessor; finite injectivity/surjectivity then excludes name replacements and blank collisions.
declarations.RDF11.finite_blank_no_proper_self_instan: A graph with finitely many occurring blanks is not a proper instance of itself. This syntactic result does not require leanness or finitely many triples.
declarations.RDF11.lean_entails_proper_gives_self_ins: If a lean graph entails one of its proper instances, interpolation gives a further instance inside the original graph. Leanness forces equality, and composition preserves properness, yielding a proper self-instance. This reduction requires no finiteness and works for generalized graphs.
declarations.RDF11.lean_proper_nonentailment_iff: For a lean graph, excluding entailment of every proper instance is exactly equivalent to excluding a proper self-instance. This isolates the unrestricted source theorem's remaining obstruction; it does not assume or prove that obstruction impossible for all infinite lean graphs.
declarations.RDF11.lean_finite_blanks_not_entails_pro: A lean graph with finitely many occurring blanks does not simply entail a proper instance of itself. Both graphs may have generalized syntax, and the triple set may be infinite. The specification states the consequence without the finite-blank hypothesis; that unrestricted scope remains open.
declarations.RDF11.lean_finite_graph_not_entails_prop: The finite-graph corollary: a lean finite graph does not simply entail a proper instance. It follows from the stronger finite-blank-support theorem and the proved blank enumeration construction.
declarations.RDF11.InfiniteProperInstance.triple: The ordinary triple with subject blank n, fixed IRI predicate p and fixed IRI object o. It is a component of a constructed source-review example, not an example printed in the specification.
declarations.RDF11.InfiniteProperInstance.graph: The ordinary graph containing one such triple for every natural-number blank identity. The triples form a set, with fixed predicate and object.
declarations.RDF11.InfiniteProperInstance.hasBlank: Every natural-number blank occurs as a subject in the example graph.
declarations.RDF11.InfiniteProperInstance.fold: Map blank n to blank floor(n/2). Adjacent identities collide, while every natural-number output still has a predecessor. This is a proper simultaneous substitution on the example.
declarations.RDF11.InfiniteProperInstance.fold_triple: Substituting in the example triple replaces only its subject index by floor(n/2); its named predicate and object remain fixed.
declarations.RDF11.InfiniteProperInstance.fold_image: Despite identifying adjacent blank nodes, folding maps the entire infinite graph onto exactly itself. The even index 2n supplies a predecessor for each output triple.
declarations.RDF11.InfiniteProperInstance.fold_proper: The fold is proper because occurring blanks 0 and 1 are distinct but have the same replacement.
declarations.RDF11.InfiniteProperInstance.proper_self: The constructed infinite ordinary graph is a proper instance of itself with literal set equality. It is also proved non-lean, so this is not a counterexample to the specification's lean-graph theorem.
declarations.RDF11.InfiniteProperInstance.infinite_bl: The example has no finite enumeration of its occurring blank nodes: every natural number occurs, so the existing infinitude theorem applies.
declarations.RDF11.InfiniteProperInstance.infinite_gr: The example has no finite triple enumeration, since such an enumeration would give finite blank support, which has already been excluded.
declarations.RDF11.InfiniteProperInstance.not_lean: The example is non-lean: replacing all blanks by blank 0 produces a singleton proper subgraph. This guard prevents treating the example as a refutation of the source's theorem about lean graphs.
declarations.RDF11.Statements.lean_proper_instance_fi: Headline alias for the checked finite-blank scope: a lean graph with finitely many occurring blanks does not simply entail a proper instance. Generalized syntax and infinite triple sets are permitted. The source's unrestricted statement remains open.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSDerives.domain: Compose two existing derivations using rdfs2: a derived domain assertion and a derived property edge produce subject class typing. The underlying rule soundness keeps one assignment throughout.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSDerives.range: Compose a derived range assertion and property edge using rdfs3 to type the object, retaining the same derivation context and assignment.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSDerives.subclass: Compose a derived subclass assertion and class membership using rdfs9. This is a proof helper over the existing rule, not an additional axiom.
declarations.RDF11.rdfsAdditionalClassSymbols: The twelve core subjects in the source table of additional class typings, in source order. XMLLiteral and HTML are deliberately separate because their proofs currently require recognition in D. This list is not exhaustive of all valid class typings.
declarations.RDF11.rdfsAdditionalPropertySymbols: The nine subjects listed with rdf:Property type in the additional-valid-triples table. Their validity is proved from existing axioms and rules.
declarations.RDF11.rdfs_domain_axiom_derivable: Insert a member of the already transcribed domain-axiom family into an RDFS derivation. Membership in that existing family is required.
declarations.RDF11.rdfs_range_axiom_derivable: Insert an existing range axiom into an RDFS derivation, with explicit membership evidence.
declarations.RDF11.rdfs_hierarchy_axiom_derivable: Insert an existing hierarchy axiom into an RDFS derivation. It does not extend the axiom table.
declarations.RDF11.rdfs_domain_target_class_derivable: A class appearing as the target of a vocabulary domain axiom has rdfs:Class type, using the declared range of rdfs:domain.
declarations.RDF11.rdfs_range_target_class_derivable: A class appearing as the target of a vocabulary range axiom has rdfs:Class type, using the declared range of rdfs:range.
declarations.RDF11.rdfs_additional_class_derivable: Derive each of the twelve core class typings from domain/range and hierarchy axioms; ContainerMembershipProperty uses a member of the full indexed container family. None of these consequences is assumed as an extra axiom.
declarations.RDF11.rdfs_recognized_datatype_class_der: A recognized datatype is typed rdfs:Datatype and is consequently a class. The recognition premise is essential to the statement; this does not settle the source table's unqualified XMLLiteral/HTML entries.
declarations.RDF11.rdfs_domain_property_derivable: A vocabulary property having a listed domain is typed rdf:Property through the domain of rdfs:domain.
declarations.RDF11.rdfs_additional_property_derivable: Every one of the nine additional property typings has a derivation through its existing domain axiom. The proof does not assume the conclusion table.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSVocabulary.additionalClassTrip: The set of the twelve core class-typing conclusions. This graph excludes the two optional-datatype entries whose unqualified validity is still under review.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSVocabulary.additionalPropertyT: The set of the nine property-typing conclusions printed in the source table, represented as generalized triples with fixed IRI terms.
declarations.RDF11.rdfs_additional_types_entailed: Every premise graph RDFS-entails the twelve core class typings. Existing derivation soundness proves the semantic consequence; this is not a completeness claim for all RDFS typing.
declarations.RDF11.rdfs_additional_properties_entaile: Every premise graph, including the empty graph, RDFS-entails all nine listed property typings. The result holds in every RDFS model through the previously checked rule soundness theorem.
declarations.RDF11.rdfs_recognized_datatype_class_ent: Any recognized datatype IRI has an RDFS-entailed rdfs:Class typing. Instantiating this for XMLLiteral or HTML requires its recognition in D; the printed table omits that qualifier and remains under review.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.rdfs_class_se: In every RDFS model, the resource denoted by rdfs:Class belongs to its own class extension. This is a universal consequence of the axioms and rules, stronger than a single model permitting self-membership.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.rdfs_resource: In every RDFS model, the extension of rdfs:Resource has a member because it equals the nonempty resource universe. Empty-class permission does not allow this particular class to be empty.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.unnamed_empt: The extra unnamed resource is a class whose extension is exactly empty in the constructed RDFS family. Being in IC does not require having members. Named schema columns and datatype value-space columns keep their existing meanings.
declarations.RDF11.RDFSModelConstruction.empty_class_: Under the existing sufficient constructor Parameters, exhibit an actual RDFS interpretation with an empty class. No empty-datatype-space premise is needed. This is a permitted configuration, not a condition requiring every interpretation to contain an empty class.
declarations.RDF11.Term.mapNames: Change IRI and literal names through the two supplied maps, retaining every blank identity. The map may identify names; no injectivity or cross-edition semantic compatibility is asserted.
declarations.RDF11.Subject.mapNames: Change the IRI of an ordinary subject while leaving a blank subject unchanged; literal subjects remain impossible in this type.
declarations.RDF11.Triple.mapNames: Map the names of an ordinary triple without changing its ordinary subject/predicate restrictions or blank identities.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.mapNames: Apply the same name maps to all three positions, keeping the existing generalized syntax.
declarations.RDF11.Graph.mapNames: The set image of an ordinary graph under name mapping. If two triples become equal, they are one member of the resulting set.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedGraph.mapNames: The set image of a generalized graph under name mapping. Blank sharing is preserved and graph sethood is retained.
declarations.RDF11.Triple.generalize_mapNames: Changing names and embedding an ordinary triple into generalized syntax commute. The helper therefore also applies to ordinary RDF triples.
declarations.RDF11.Graph.generalize_mapNames: Changing names commutes with the ordinary-to-generalized graph embedding, connecting the transport proof to ordinary RDF syntax.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.comapNames: Interpret source names through their supplied target-name maps. Keep IR, IP, IEXT and the same resource carrier; partial literal denotation stays partial. This is a simple interpretation, not a certificate of RDF/RDFS or version compatibility.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.denote_mapNam: A mapped term has exactly the denotation supplied by the pulled-back interpretation, with the same blank assignment and including undefined denotations.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.tripleTrue_ma: Truth of a mapped triple equals truth in the pulled-back interpretation for the same assignment. No total-literal or property-as-resource assumption is added.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.graphTrue_map: All triples retain truth under one common assignment across the graph. This preserves correlations from shared blank nodes.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.satisfies_map: Name transport preserves existential graph satisfaction through interpretation pullback, using the existing proof that assignments can be restricted to exactly the occurring blanks.
declarations.RDF11.simplyEntails_mapNames: A simple entailment remains valid after the same IRI and literal maps are applied to both graphs. This is the forward direction for arbitrary maps; it does not assert reflection when names collapse.
declarations.RDF11.VocabularyIRI: An ambient IRI together with evidence that this IRI name belongs to V. It is not a newly parsed or normalized IRI spelling.
declarations.RDF11.VocabularyLiteral: An ambient literal together with evidence that its literal name belongs to V. Literal identity remains distinct from equality of denoted values.
declarations.RDF11.PreInterpretation: Reuse the normative simple-interpretation structure on the names admitted by V. IS still maps into IR or IP, IL is partial, and IR is nonempty. Appendix B describes the codomain more loosely; this precise refinement is awaiting source review. Neither V nor IR is required to be finite here.
declarations.RDF11.PreInterpretation.extend: Complete a pre-interpretation to all ambient names. Preserve IR, IP, IEXT and existing name denotations; send unused IRIs to one existing resource and leave unused literals undefined. This construction proves simple-semantic completion, not datatype/RDF/RDFS completion.
declarations.RDF11.PreInterpretation.restrict_extend: Completing the name mappings and restricting back to V recovers the original interpretation exactly, including partial literal values and the resource/property distinction.
declarations.RDF11.PreInterpretation.denote_extend: Every term over V keeps exactly the same denotation under completion and the same assignment, including an undefined literal result.
declarations.RDF11.PreInterpretation.tripleTrue_exten: Every triple over V has the same truth value before and after name completion, for each fixed blank assignment.
declarations.RDF11.PreInterpretation.graphTrue_extend: The whole graph has the same truth value under each fixed assignment. Shared blanks use one common witness across its triples; this is stronger than separate singleton-triple satisfaction.
declarations.RDF11.PreInterpretation.satisfies_extend: A graph over V is satisfied by the completion exactly when the original pre-interpretation satisfies it, preserving existential blank-node meaning.
declarations.RDF11.PreInterpretation.satisfies_of_res: Any interpretation on the same carrier whose restriction is exactly the given pre-interpretation preserves satisfaction of graphs over V. The equality premise retains IR, IP, IEXT and the known name mappings.
declarations.RDF11.PreInterpretation.satisfiable_iff: A graph over V has a pre-interpretation model exactly when its inclusion into ambient names has a full simple model. Both directions use explicit restriction or completion, not a finite-carrier assertion.
declarations.RDF11.PreInterpretation.entails_iff: Simple entailment between graphs on restricted name types is equivalent to entailment between their ambient inclusions. The left side ranges over all V-preinterpretations; their resource carriers may be infinite.
declarations.RDF11.Term.restrictNames: Place an ambient term in the restricted name types using proof that its names occur in V. A literal contributes both itself and its datatype IRI to that proof requirement; blanks are unchanged.
declarations.RDF11.Term.include_restrictNames: Including a restricted term back into ambient names recovers the exact original term, not merely an equal denotation.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.restrictNames: Restrict all three terms using the triple-vocabulary evidence, without changing its blank identities.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.include_restrict: The ambient inclusion of the restricted triple is exactly the original triple.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedGraph.restrictNames: Represent a graph over V by restricting the names in each of its triples, with an explicit vocabulary-containment premise. The result is a set and preserves all blank sharing.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedGraph.include_restrictN: Including the restricted graph into ambient names recovers the original triple set exactly.
declarations.RDF11.preinterpretation_entailment_iff: For ambient graphs whose names are all in V, simple entailment is equivalent to entailment between their restricted-name representations. This uses all pre-interpretations, not just finite-resource ones; the two graphs may have different blank domains.
declarations.RDF11.preinterpretation_satisfiable_iff: Restricting a graph to a vocabulary containing its names preserves and reflects simple satisfiability. No resource-cardinality bound is claimed.
