declarations.RDF11.Term.nameList: A finite list of the names contributed by one term: an IRI contributes itself, a literal itself and its datatype IRI, and a blank contributes none. Later enumeration removes repeated names.
declarations.RDF11.Term.mem_nameList: The finite term-name list has exactly the membership of the existing set-valued names definition.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.nameList: Concatenate the name contributions of the three triple positions. Intermediate repetition is allowed; this list is not the semantic graph or a certified enumeration.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.mem_nameList: The triple-name list contains exactly the names defined by the existing triple-vocabulary predicate.
declarations.RDF11.finite_vocabulary_of_finite_graph: A finite graph has a finite name vocabulary, with an exact membership proof and duplicate-free enumeration. Literal datatype IRIs are included even when not separate triple terms.
declarations.RDF11.finite_shared_vocabulary: Two finite graphs have an exactly enumerated union vocabulary. This is the comparison vocabulary suggested by Appendix B; it counts names, not distinct denotations.
declarations.RDF11.finite_vocabulary_comparison: Combine exact finite comparison vocabulary with preservation and reflection of simple entailment. This theorem still quantifies over unrestricted resource domains; separate bounded-countermodel theorems now establish the N+B+1 bound.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.DomainRestric: Evidence for keeping a selected set of active objects: retain one resource for nonemptiness, every IRI denotation, and every defined literal denotation. This construction is for simple semantics and does not assert that RDF/RDFS conditions survive restriction.

Intersect both IR and IP with the kept set and restrict IEXT to the retained resources. Preserve name values, undefined literals and the distinction between resource and property roles; an object outside IR is never made a resource.
Forget only the evidence that assigned resources are in the kept set. The original resource values and blank identities do not change.
Each term has the same denotation in the restricted interpretation and in the original under the lifted assignment, including undefined results.
Any defined denotation obtained in the restricted interpretation belongs to the kept set, including predicate-only IRI values.
For a restricted assignment, each triple is true exactly when it is true in the original interpretation under the same values. This does not say every original assignment fits in the smaller domain.
Lift one common assignment across the entire graph; all its triples retain their truth. Correlations between shared blanks are preserved.
A graph satisfied by the restricted model is satisfied by the original. Consequently, an originally false conclusion cannot become true merely through this restriction.
Retain an original assignment in the restricted model when every defined value is proved to belong to the kept set. Undefined entries remain undefined.
Restricting a supported assignment and forgetting its membership evidence recovers the exact original assignment.
If all values of one satisfying premise assignment are retained, the whole premise remains satisfied after restriction. No second positive witness for the conclusion is required.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration.subset: Filter an exact duplicate-free enumeration to a proved subset. Membership stays exact, and filtering cannot introduce duplicates.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration.subset_length: A subset enumeration has no more entries than the original enumeration.
declarations.RDF11.Enumeration.fromList_length: Removing repeated input values yields an exact enumeration whose length is at most the original list length. Intermediate lists may repeat; the certified result cannot.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.BoundedDomain: There is an exact duplicate-free enumeration of all objects in IR or IP, with at most n entries. Overlap is counted once. The ambient Lean type may contain unused objects; this bound concerns the active semantic domain.
The active-domain bound also bounds IR, by taking its subset enumeration. This supplies Appendix B's resource-universe bound even when some properties lie outside IR.
declarations.RDF11.FiniteSimpleModel.nameValue: Obtain an IRI name's denotation or a literal name's optional denotation. Undefined literals contribute no value to the finite support.
declarations.RDF11.FiniteSimpleModel.nameValue_active: Every defined name value is a resource or property in the original interpretation. This retains property-only referents rather than assuming IP is a subset of IR.
declarations.RDF11.FiniteSimpleModel.values: Collect the comparison names' defined values, assignment values for the enumerated blank identities, and one existing resource. Only counted blanks enter the list; unused ambient assignments are not collected.
declarations.RDF11.FiniteSimpleModel.values_length: The support list has at most N+B+1 entries: at most one value per enumerated name, one per enumerated blank, and one resource for nonemptiness. Identical values may reduce the eventual distinct count.
declarations.RDF11.FiniteSimpleModel.name_kept: Every defined value of a name in the comparison vocabulary is included in the support list.
declarations.RDF11.FiniteSimpleModel.assignment_kept: The value assigned to a counted blank identity is retained. The occurrence/coverage premise is essential to the cardinality bound.
declarations.RDF11.FiniteSimpleModel.values_active: Every selected support value already belongs to IR or IP. Restriction introduces no new resource or property membership.
declarations.RDF11.FiniteSimpleModel.restriction: Build the supported restriction of the original interpretation on the comparison vocabulary. Keep its name denotations and use the chosen resource to retain nonemptiness.
declarations.RDF11.FiniteSimpleModel.restriction_boun: The restricted interpretation has an exact enumeration of IR union IP with at most N+B+1 distinct objects. The proof uses list-length bounds and duplicate removal, not a unique-name assumption.
declarations.RDF11.FiniteSimpleModel.compress: From a model of G, construct a full-name model with at most N+B+1 active objects that still satisfies G. Any conclusion over the selected vocabulary satisfied by the new model is satisfied by the original. Thus original conclusion falsity is preserved; arbitrary original positive graphs need not survive.
declarations.RDF11.bounded_simple_countermodel: Failure of simple entailment yields a bounded model satisfying the premise and falsifying the conclusion. The vocabulary covers both graphs; the counted blanks need cover only the premise's occurring blanks.
declarations.RDF11.simple_entailment_iff_bounded: Checking all models with the stated active-domain bound is equivalent to the existing unrestricted simple entailment definition. This is a semantic equivalence, not an implemented decision algorithm.
declarations.RDF11.simple_satisfiable_iff_bounded: Simple satisfiability is equivalent to existence of a model with the N+B+1 active-domain bound, using explicit vocabulary and blank-support enumerations.
declarations.RDF11.simple_entailment_iff_bounded_prei: Appendix B's bounded comparison: use exactly the union vocabulary and union of occurring blank identities. Entailment holds exactly when every pre-interpretation with at most N+B+1 active objects preserves truth from G to E. Shared blank identities do not force the two satisfaction witnesses to agree.
declarations.RDF11.simple_satisfiable_iff_bounded_pre: A graph is simply satisfiable exactly when its restricted-name representation has a pre-interpretation model with the comparison's N+B+1 active-domain bound. Name completion connects the restricted and full models.
declarations.RDF11.finite_shared_blank_support: Finite input graphs supply an exact duplicate-free enumeration of the union of their occurring blank identities. A blank shared by both graphs is counted once.
declarations.RDF11.finite_simple_countermodel: For finite G and E, produce the exact comparison-name and shared-blank enumerations and an N+B+1 countermodel whenever simple entailment fails. The completed interpretation maps all names, while its active semantic domain is bounded.
declarations.RDF11.Statements.finite_simple_countermo: Headline review alias for Appendix B's simple finite-model bound: finite graphs that do not entail one another have a countermodel with at most N+B+1 active objects. N and B are exact enumeration lengths, including datatype IRI names and shared blank identities. All hypotheses are inherited from the proved theorem.
declarations.RDF11.PreInterpretation.DConditions: The localized datatype conditions use the original external meanings. Recognized IRI names present in V denote their fixed datatypes. Only literals in V require the corresponding language-pair or lexical-to-value result; recognized ill-typed literals stay undefined. This is a precise proposed reading of Appendix B, not a proof of full-model completion.
declarations.RDF11.PreInterpretation.DModel: There is one coherent partial realization of datatype values for which all localized conditions hold. Sharing this realization preserves alias equality and keeps distinct realized values distinct.
declarations.RDF11.PreInterpretation.conditions_of_fu: Restricting the names of any full D-interpretation gives a pre-interpretation satisfying the localized datatype conditions, with exactly the same external value realization.
declarations.RDF11.PreInterpretation.conditions_full_: When V contains every IRI and every literal, the localized conditions are exactly equivalent to the original full datatype conditions. Thus the weakening comes from restricting the name domain, not from changing the prescribed datatype meanings.
declarations.RDF11.PreInterpretation.conditions_empty: With no recognized datatypes, every pre-interpretation meets the localized datatype conditions using an everywhere-undefined value realization.
declarations.RDF11.PreInterpretation.recognized_alias: Two recognized vocabulary IRIs identifying the same external datatype have the same denotation in the pre-interpretation. Localization does not permit inconsistent alias meanings.
declarations.RDF11.PreInterpretation.illTyped_undefin: A recognized ill-typed literal present in the vocabulary has no local denotation. Removing global value-space obligations does not allow inventing a value for it.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.DomainRestric: A supported domain restriction preserves exactly which external value a literal denotes, with the same realization. Retained resource evidence changes, but the denotation and prescribed value do not.
A literal is undefined after supported domain restriction exactly when it was undefined before. No missing value is filled in or existing literal value discarded.
declarations.RDF11.PreInterpretation.conditions_domai: Keeping all local name values and one resource preserves every localized datatype condition under the existing restriction of IR, IP and IEXT. This makes the simple finite-support construction usable for weakened datatype models.
declarations.RDF11.Term.literal_in_names: An occurring literal contributes its literal name to the vocabulary of its term. Its datatype IRI is also included by the existing names definition.
declarations.RDF11.GeneralizedTriple.literal_in_names: A literal occurring in any triple position belongs to that triple's vocabulary. This permits the same argument for ordinary and generalized graphs.
declarations.RDF11.d_satisfiable_of_preinterpretation: If a local datatype model satisfies the restricted graph, no occurring literal can be recognized and ill-typed. The existing full D-model construction then witnesses satisfiability. It builds a new model; it does not preserve the original local relation or other graph truths.
declarations.RDF11.FiniteDatatypeModel.compress: From a full D-model satisfying G, keep comparison-name values, the values of one premise blank assignment, and one resource. The result has at most N+B+1 active objects, retains localized datatype conditions, satisfies restricted G, and reflects every conclusion over V into the original model. It need not preserve other original positive graphs.
declarations.RDF11.bounded_d_pre_countermodel: If full D-entailment fails, there is a weakened pre-interpretation countermodel with at most N+B+1 active objects. For unrestricted generalized conclusions this is only one direction: a local countermodel need not refute full D-entailment. A separate completion theorem proves the converse for ordinary conclusions; the checked generalized example explains that restriction.
declarations.RDF11.d_entailment_of_bounded_preinterpr: If every bounded weakened model satisfying G also satisfies E, then full D-entailment holds. For unrestricted generalized conclusions this remains a sufficient criterion. A separate completion theorem proves the equivalence for ordinary conclusions. Neither result supplies an executable decision procedure.
declarations.RDF11.bounded_d_pre_model_of_satisfiable: A full D-model of G supplies a bounded weakened pre-model over any finite vocabulary covering G and finite support covering its blanks. The count is N+B+1, without enumerating the recognized datatype set.
declarations.RDF11.d_satisfiable_iff_bounded_preinter: D-satisfiability is equivalent to existence of a weakened pre-model with at most N+B+1 active objects. Compression proves one direction; absence of ill-typed literals and a separate full-model construction prove the other. This does not give entailment-preserving completion.
declarations.RDF11.finite_d_pre_countermodel: Finite G and E supply exact enumerations of their union vocabulary and shared occurring blank identities. Any full D-countermodel then yields a weakened countermodel with N+B+1 active objects. Full datatype completion and the printed multiplicative bound remain open.
declarations.RDF11.FiniteDatatypeModel.resource_enume: Every exact finite enumeration of a section-5 resource universe has positive length, because IR contains at least one resource.
declarations.RDF11.FiniteDatatypeModel.no_zero_resour: No simple interpretation or pre-interpretation retaining nonempty IR can have a resource enumeration of length at most zero.
declarations.RDF11.FiniteDatatypeModel.empty_comparis: Comparing two empty graphs gives exactly zero vocabulary names and zero occurring blank identities. Recognizing datatypes does not automatically insert their names into either graph.

The empty graph has a full D-model, but its zero name and blank counts make the printed (N+B)*(d+1) resource bound impossible for any nonempty-IR pre-interpretation, whatever finite d is used. This is a checked source-review boundary under our precise refinement, not an adopted erratum.
declarations.RDF11.Statements.datatype_preinterpretat: Headline alias for the derived datatype satisfiability equivalence under localized conditions and the N+B+1 active-domain bound. It inherits the complete theorem type; it does not claim the printed multiplicative bound or datatype entailment equivalence.
declarations.RDF11.ValueRealization.embed: Extend a partial realization into a larger carrier. Reuse the embedded old object for an already realized value; give each previously unrealized value its own right-hand tagged object.
declarations.RDF11.ValueRealization.embed_of_defined: An already realized external value keeps exactly its old object under the left-hand embedding.
declarations.RDF11.ValueRealization.embed_injective: Distinct external values stay distinct after completion. Existing realized values use the original injectivity proof, and newly supplied values have distinct tagged representatives.
declarations.RDF11.ValueRealization.complete: Make the value realization total in U plus Value while preserving injectivity. This can enlarge the carrier without identifying previously distinct datatype values.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletion.iriValue: Keep every vocabulary IRI's old denotation. Interpret an absent recognized datatype IRI by its fixed completed datatype value, and use an existing resource for other absent IRIs.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletion.literalValue: Supply recognized literal values globally from the fixed datatype theory, including normalized language pairs and undefined ill-typed literals. Preserve local unrecognized literal values and leave absent unrecognized literals undefined.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletion.interpretation: Build a full-name simple interpretation on U plus Value. IR and IP are universal as a constructor choice; the only relation edges are embedded old edges with their old resource/property evidence. Name values and global datatype evaluation are handled separately.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletion.iriValue_local: Every IRI present in the local vocabulary keeps its old denotation, embedded into the larger carrier.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletion.iriValue_recogn: Every globally recognized datatype IRI denotes its fixed completed datatype identity, whether or not its name was in the local vocabulary.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletion.literalValue_la: A recognized tagged literal receives the completed value of its lexical string and normalized language tag.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletion.literalValue_or: A recognized non-language literal uses exactly the fixed lexical-to-value evaluation, including an undefined result.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletion.literalValue_lo: The local datatype conditions ensure that every vocabulary literal keeps its previous optional denotation under the embedding. Global completion does not silently repair an undefined local literal.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletion.conditions: The completed interpretation satisfies every full datatype condition with the completed value realization. This checks global IRI identity and both literal-evaluation cases, not just the literals appearing in the input graphs.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletion.relates_iff: A completed relation edge exists exactly when all three values are embedded old values forming an old relation edge. Universal completed IR/IP do not create additional edges.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletion.liftAssignment: Embed each defined old blank-node assignment into the completed resource universe, retaining blank identities and undefined entries.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletion.denote_lift: Under the embedded assignment, each local term denotes exactly its embedded old value, or remains undefined. The same assignment is used throughout the graph.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletion.tripleTrue_lift: Every generalized triple retains its truth under the same embedded old assignment. This does not say that all new assignments in the larger resource universe come from old assignments.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletion.graphTrue_lift_: A whole generalized graph retains truth under one common embedded assignment. Shared blank-node correlations are preserved across all its triples.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletion.satisfies_forwa: Every locally satisfied generalized graph remains satisfied in the completed full model. The reverse direction is not asserted for unrestricted generalized graphs.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletion.lowerAssignment: Keep only assigned values that are embedded old resources. Drop new values and old property-only values. In an ordinary satisfied graph, relation endpoints ensure that every occurring blank survives this restriction.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletion.denote_reflect_: If a completed term denotes an embedded old resource, it has the same old denotation under the lowered assignment. The old-resource premise is essential for blank nodes.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletion.ordinary_triple: A true completed ordinary triple is true locally under the lowered assignment. Its predicate is a fixed IRI, and its subject/object relation endpoints are old resources; no new predicate-blank witness can appear in this syntax.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletion.ordinary_satisf: The completion satisfies an ordinary graph exactly when the local model does. One lowered assignment works for the entire graph. The corresponding unrestricted generalized statement is refuted by the separate scope example.
declarations.RDF11.d_entailment_iff_preinterpretation: Full datatype entailment of an ordinary conclusion is equivalent to preservation of truth over all localized datatype pre-models. The premise may be generalized. Completion proves one direction and restriction of full models proves the other.
declarations.RDF11.d_entailment_iff_bounded_preinterp: For an ordinary conclusion, it suffices and is necessary to check all localized datatype pre-models with at most N+B+1 active objects. Vocabulary covers both graphs and counted blanks cover the premise. This is a model-theoretic equivalence, not an executable search algorithm or the printed multiplicative bound.
declarations.RDF11.Subject.restrictNames: Move an ordinary subject into the selected vocabulary while retaining its IRI or blank form. The occurrence evidence supplies the IRI's membership proof.
declarations.RDF11.Subject.toTerm_restrictNames: Restricting an ordinary subject and then viewing it as a term agrees with restricting its term representation.
declarations.RDF11.Triple.restrictNames: Restrict the names of an ordinary triple while keeping its subject and predicate position restrictions. The predicate remains an IRI.
declarations.RDF11.Triple.generalize_restrictNames: Generalization and vocabulary restriction commute for ordinary triples, so the existing generalized proofs apply without losing the ordinary syntax guarantee.
declarations.RDF11.Graph.restrictNames: Restrict all names of an ordinary graph using their vocabulary membership evidence. Collect the resulting ordinary triples as a set, retaining shared blank identities.
declarations.RDF11.Graph.generalize_restrictNames: Restricting an ordinary graph and then generalizing gives exactly the existing generalized restriction. This connects ordinary completion to the earlier finite compression theorem.
declarations.RDF11.SimpleInterpretation.datatype_name: If a recognized literal has a recognized datatype object as its value, the IRI identifying that object must denote a resource in every full D-model. The literal may be absent from the graphs being compared.
declarations.RDF11.d_predicate_blank_of_datatype_valu: When global datatype conditions force the predicate IRI's denotation into IR, a named-predicate triple D-entails the corresponding generalized triple with a predicate blank. That blank can use the forced resource.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletionScope.Iri: Four abstract names for the scope witness: an endpoint, a predicate that identifies a datatype, another datatype, and the language datatype. These are example symbols, not asserted concrete RDF vocabulary IRIs.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletionScope.Value: The example value domain keeps language string/tag pairs separate from four datatype descriptors. A descriptor can itself be a value of another custom datatype.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletionScope.theory: An abstract custom datatype theory with one ambient literal. Its datatype evaluates that literal to the descriptor identified by the predicate name; the literal and its datatype name are absent from the comparison vocabulary. Language-value injectivity and the exceptional missing language L2V are retained.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletionScope.recognized: Recognize the predicate's datatype identity and the datatype of the omitted literal. The endpoint and language names are unrecognized in this example.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletionScope.vocabulary: The local vocabulary contains just the endpoint and predicate IRI names. It contains no literal and no name for the omitted literal's datatype.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletionScope.node: The endpoint name together with its proof of membership in the local vocabulary.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletionScope.property: The predicate name together with its local vocabulary membership proof. It identifies a recognized datatype in this example.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletionScope.premise: The local singleton graph s p s, with fixed IRI endpoints and predicate. Its syntax is ground and ordinary.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletionScope.conclusion: The local singleton generalized graph s _:b s. Its predicate blank must receive a resource value; this position would be forbidden in an ordinary RDF triple.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletionScope.premodel: The local Boolean model has false as its sole resource and true as its sole property. The predicate denotes true, the endpoint denotes false, and the sole possible property edge holds. The property is outside IR.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletionScope.realizatio: Realize the predicate's fixed datatype descriptor as true and leave other external values unrealized locally. The realization is injective wherever it is defined.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletionScope.local_cond: The example pre-model satisfies every current localized datatype condition. The recognized local predicate has its fixed referent; no local literal creates a value obligation.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletionScope.premise_tr: The local pre-model satisfies the named-predicate premise using its true property and false endpoint.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletionScope.conclusion: The local pre-model cannot satisfy the predicate-blank conclusion. Every blank must denote false in IR, while every property denotes true.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletionScope.premodel_b: The entire active domain of the counterexample has an exact two-element enumeration. The obstruction is already present in a finite local model.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletionScope.premise_in: Including the vocabulary names gives exactly the full-domain singleton s p s, with no extra triple or premise.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletionScope.conclusion: Including the vocabulary names gives exactly the full-domain singleton s _:b s, preserving the existential predicate blank.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletionScope.comparison: The selected vocabulary is exactly the union of the two compared graphs' vocabularies, including the usual datatype-IRI accounting. It does not omit a name actually present in either graph.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletionScope.global_lit: The global literal forcing resource membership is absent from the comparison vocabulary. This is why its value obligation is missing locally.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletionScope.full_premi: The ground premise has a full D-model under the same datatype theory. The full entailment below is therefore not a vacuous consequence of an inconsistent premise.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletionScope.literal_fo: The omitted recognized literal evaluates to exactly the fixed datatype object identified by the predicate IRI. This supplies the global resource-membership obligation.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletionScope.full_entai: Every full D-model of s p s satisfies s _:b s: global literal evaluation makes p's denotation a resource available to the predicate blank.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletionScope.no_compari: No full D-model can preserve both local satisfaction values of this comparison, even allowing a different carrier. This refutes unrestricted generalized comparison preservation for the chosen localized conditions, while leaving other possible refinements of the source sketch open.
declarations.RDF11.Statements.datatype_preinterpretat: Headline alias for the bounded datatype entailment equivalence with an ordinary conclusion. The complete type retains the vocabulary and blank-support covers, N+B+1 bound, generalized premise allowance and ordinary conclusion restriction.
declarations.RDF11.DatatypeCompletionScope.recognized: Both recognized custom datatypes have nonempty value spaces. The scope obstruction does not rely on an empty datatype; the predicate datatype evaluates to a fixed string/tag pair, and the omitted literal's datatype evaluates to the predicate datatype object.
